chunks: Yunus from Al-A'ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The servant will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment with blood moistening him, so something resembling a cupping cup or more than that would be handed over to him, and it would be said to him, 'This is your share from the blood of so-and-so.' So he would say, 'O Lord, You know that You caused me to die and I had not spilled any blood.' So He would say, 'Yes, you heard a report of such and such from so-and-so, and you reported it upon him, and it was transmitted until it came to so-and-so the tyrant, and he was killed because of it, and this is your share from his blood.'

key_terms.الْمِحْجَمَةِ: The cupping cup (a measure of blood)

ai.seo_question: How does transmitting knowledge lead to bearing the blood of the killed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanism of 'sharing in the blood' (sahm min damihi) by tracing the chain of transmission from a scholar to a ruler, highlighting how the mere act of publicizing knowledge can lead to martyrdom. It underscores the spiritual accountability of the narrator, distinguishing between direct killing and the indirect consequence of one's report reaching a tyrant, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence of knowledge transmission.
